title: Universal Life Insurance Loan Administration Rate Table
content:
Policy loans on Ashgrove Universal Life Insurance carry the charged and credited rates and the limits below for each tier. The charged rate is the annual interest rate on the loan; the credited rate is the annual rate credited on the part of the account value held as collateral for the loan.

## Rate and limit table

| Item | Lifetime Guarantee UL | Protection UL | Accumulation UL | Indexed UL Protect | Indexed UL Growth | Indexed UL Premier |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standard loan charged rate | 5% | 5% | 5% | 5% | 5% | 5% |
| Standard loan credited rate on collateral | 3% | 3% | 3% | 3% | 3% | 3% |
| Preferred loan first policy year | 11 | 11 | 11 | 11 | 11 | 6 |
| Preferred loan charged rate | 3% | 3% | 3% | 3% | 3% | 3% |
| Preferred loan credited rate on collateral | 3% | 3% | 3% | 3% | 3% | 3% |
| Share of the cash surrender value (before loans) total indebtedness may reach when a loan is taken | 90% | 90% | 90% | 90% | 90% | 90% |
| Smallest new loan | $500 | $500 | $500 | $500 | $500 | $500 |
| Smallest repayment, unless it repays the loan in full | $50 | $50 | $50 | $50 | $50 | $50 |

As decimals: standard charged 0.05, standard and preferred credited 0.03, preferred charged 0.03, loan limit share 0.90.

## Notes

- The preferred loan first policy year is the first policy year in which loans are treated as preferred loans. On the Ashgrove Indexed UL Premier it is policy year 6; on every other tier it is policy year 11. Policy year 6 begins on the fifth policy anniversary and policy year 11 on the tenth.
- A repayment of less than $50 is below the smallest repayment unless it pays the loan off in full.

## Hypothetical figures

An Ashgrove Indexed UL Premier policy in policy year 7 is in its preferred loan years (from policy year 6); an Ashgrove Indexed UL Growth policy in the same policy year is not (its preferred loan years begin in policy year 11). A requested new loan of $300.00 is below the $500 smallest loan on every tier.
